newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina signs oil contracts with foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina signs oil contracts with foreign firms.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina signed eight oil and gas production sharing contracts with foreign oil companies, including a unit of Carmanah Resources Ltd, on Thursday, a Pertamina spokesman said.
Under the contract, GFB Resources Indonesia, a wholly owned unit of Carmanah, will invest $96 milion to explore a block offshore North East Natuna, in the South China Sea, the spokesman said.

Pertamina also signed production sharing contracts with Japan Petroleum Exploration Co (JAPEX), Indonesia Petroleum Ltd (INPEX), both of Japan, Apache Corp of the United States and units of Australia's City View Corp, New Zealand's Cue Energy Resources unit and Total of France.

According to the contracts, INPEX will invest $96 million to explore in the Rabe block offshore East Timor while JAPEX will spend $157 million to search for gas and oil in the Sabo block, offshore south Timor.
Apache will explore in an onshore block at Korinci-Baru in Riau, Central Sumatra, with an investment of $19.7 million.
Western Madura Pty Ltd, a wholly owned unit of City View, will invest $63 million on exploration in the Madura area of East Java province, the contracts said.
Cue Energy, in a joint venture with Indonesia's Wirabuana Petrolindo Ltd, will explore offshore Tanjung Jabung in the southern part of Sumatra island.
Total signed two production sharing contracts with Pertamina. It will explore in Sebawang block II, offshore East Kalimantan, and also in the nearby block of Saliki.
Pertamina also signed four Technical Assistance Contracts (TACs) with local and foreign companies.
